bottom_line: In stable coronary artery disease with preserved left ventricular function, trandolapril vs placebo did not reduce the primary end point (hazard ratio 0.96; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.88 to 1.06; P=0.43).
implications: With primary end point rates of 21.9% vs 22.5% and a hazard ratio of 0.96 (95% CI, 0.88 to 1.06; P=0.43), these data do not support a reduction in the composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal MI, or coronary revascularization from adding trandolapril to therapy in this population; however, the confidence interval remains consistent with both modest benefit and modest harm for the primary end point.

major_points.text: Double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial of trandolapril (target 4 mg/day) vs placebo in 8290 patients.
major_points.quote: The trial was a double- blind, placebo-controlled study in which 8290 patients were randomly assigned to receive either trandolapril at a target dose of 4 mg per day (4158 patients) or matching placebo (4132 patients).

major_points.text: Primary end point was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or coronary revascularization; no significant difference between groups.
major_points.quote: The incidence of the primary end point — death from cardiovascular causes, myocardial infarction, or coronary revascularization — was 21.9 percent in the trandolapril group, as compared with 22.5 percent in the placebo group (hazard ratio in the trandolapril group, 0.96

major_points.text: Follow-up extended up to 7 years (median 4.8 years), with median follow-up 4.8 years in each group.
major_points.quote: Patients underwent randomization from November 1996 to June 2000 and were followed up for as long as 7 years (median, 4.8 years), until December 31, 2003.

major_points.text: Protocol change: the original primary end point was expanded to include coronary revascularization and sample size reduced to 8100 after feasibility concerns.
major_points.quote: In October 1997, after 1584 patients had undergone randomization, the steering committee (without any knowledge of outcome data from the trial) concluded that recruiting 14,100 patients was not feasible and expanded the primary end point to include coronary revascularization.
